about.ex: About fifty people came to the meeting.

absence.en: the fact that something is not there
absence.ex: In the absence of rain, the crops died.

accord.ex: The two countries signed a peace accord.

acknowledged.ex: She acknowledged that the plan had problems.

advance.ex: The bank will advance the money.

affected.ex: Many farms were affected by the dry summer.

agreement.ex: The two countries signed a trade agreement.

aligned.en: in agreement or close to each other

allow.ex: Parents allow their children to stay up late on Fridays.

also.ex: She speaks French and also some German.

am.en: in the morning (used after a time)
am.ex: The shop opens at 9am every day.

angry.ex: The workers were angry about their low pay.

anticipated.ex: Sales are anticipated to rise next year.

any.en: one or some, of whatever kind

apart.en: separated by a distance or difference

applicable.ex: The rule is applicable to all staff.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

around.ex: Around twenty students joined the club.

arrangement.en: a plan or agreement about how things will work
arrangement.ex: The new arrangement will start next month.

as.en: in the role of; like; when

asserted.ex: She asserted that the report was wrong.

assessment.ex: The doctor made a quick assessment.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attainable.ex: A higher score is attainable with practice.

example.en: Set goals that are challenging but attainable.
example.zh: 設定有挑戰性但可達成的目標。

note.usage: 多作補語：be attainable；常與 goal/target 連用；近義 achievable。

noteEn.usage: Often used with 'goal' or 'target': 'an attainable goal'.

noteEs.usage: Suele ir con goal/target o tras be.

noteHi.exampleTr: ऐसे लक्ष्य तय करें जो कठिन पर प्राप्य हों।

noteJa.exampleTr: 難しいが達成可能な目標を立てよう。
noteJa.usage: attainable goal/target、be attainable の形が多い。

noteKo.usage: attainable goal/target, be attainable 형태가 많다.

authority.en: an official body with power to decide
authority.ex: The local authority will fix the road.

back.en: in return; to the earlier place
back.ex: Please give the book back tomorrow.

ballot.en: a vote, or the paper used to vote
ballot.ex: Every citizen has the right to a secret ballot.

be.en: exist or have a quality; used to form the passive
be.ex: The shop will be open tomorrow.

believe.ex: Many experts believe prices will rise.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

bite.en: to start having a strong effect
bite.ex: The price rises are beginning to bite.

breakthrough.ex: Scientists made a breakthrough in cancer research.

breathing.en: taking air into and out of the body
breathing.ex: Her breathing became slow and calm.

bridge.en: reduce a difference between two things
bridge.ex: Extra classes can help bridge the learning gap.

broke.ex: The meeting broke up at midnight.

by.en: done by; not later than; to the amount of

callinan.en: Kevin Callinan, head of the union Fórsa

capable.ex: She is capable of running a big team.

certain.ex: It is not certain that the plan will work.

characterised.ex: The year was characterised by high prices.

clinched.ex: They clinched the deal late at night.

close.ex: The two sides are close to a deal.

collapsed.ex: The old bridge collapsed in the flood.

coming.ex: We will decide in the coming weeks.
coming.zh: 即將到來的（the coming days：未來幾天）

commission.en: an official group with a special job
commission.ex: The commission will report next month.

committee.en: a group chosen to deal with something

compensation.en: money paid for a loss or problem
compensation.ex: Passengers got compensation for the delay.

conceded.ex: He conceded that the plan had failed.

example.en: He conceded that he was wrong.

note.usage: concede that + 子句；也可指「讓步、認輸」。

noteHi.exampleTr: उसने माना कि वह ग़लत था।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼は自分の誤りを認めた。

concerning.ex: She asked several questions concerning the cost.

confidence.en: a feeling that things will go well
confidence.ex: Business confidence rose in the spring.

congress.en: a large organisation of groups (here, trade unions)
congress.ja: 会議（アイルランド労働組合会議）
congress.zh: 大會（Irish Congress of Trade Unions：愛爾蘭工會大會）

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerably.ex: Prices are considerably higher in the city.

constituting.ex: The cuts are constituting a real problem.

example.en: Water charges remain a contentious issue.
example.zh: 水費仍是一個有爭議的議題。

note.usage: contentious issue / point / decision；同義 controversial。

noteEs.exampleTr: Las tarifas del agua siguen siendo un tema polémico.

noteHi.exampleTr: पानी का शुल्क अब भी विवादित मुद्दा है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 水道料金は依然として論争の的だ。
noteJa.meaning: 議論を呼ぶ、物議をかもす。

convene.ex: The committee will convene again in spring.

example.en: The UN convened an emergency meeting on the crisis.
example.zh: 聯合國就這場危機召開了緊急會議。

note.usage: 主詞通常是政府、主席等主辦者；被動 be convened by 很常見。

noteEn.meaning: to bring people together for a formal meeting.
noteEn.usage: Used with 'meeting', 'summit', 'panel'; often passive: 'be convened by'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ONU convocó una reunión de emergencia sobre la crisis.
noteEs.meaning: convocar una reunión o un evento.
noteEs.usage: Suele tener como sujeto un gobierno o presidente; la pasiva be convened by es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने संकट पर एक आपात बैठक बुलाई।
noteHi.usage: आमतौर पर सरकार या अध्यक्ष बुलाते हैं; be convened by भी आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 国連はその危機について緊急会合を招集した。
noteJa.meaning: 会議などを招集・開催する。
noteJa.usage: 主語は政府や議長が多く、受動態 be convened by もよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 유엔은 그 위기에 관한 긴급 회의를 소집했다.
noteKo.usage: 주어는 주로 정부나 의장이며 수동태 be convened by도 흔하다.

council.en: an official group that makes decisions

councils.en: local governments for a town or area

covering.ex: The report, covering ten years, is long.

example.en: The company needs a credible plan to cut costs.
example.zh: 公司需要一個可信的削減成本計畫。

note.usage: 常用 a credible offer/threat/alternative；反義 incredible 意思是「難以置信的」。

noteEn.meaning: believable and good enough to be taken seriously.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa necesita un plan creíble para reducir costes.
noteEs.usage: Se usa en a credible offer/threat/alternative.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी को लागत घटाने की विश्वसनीय योजना चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: a credible offer/threat आम प्रयोग है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社にはコスト削減の信頼できる計画が必要だ。
noteJa.meaning: 信頼できる；説得力のある。
noteJa.usage: a credible offer/threat の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 회사는 비용을 줄일 믿을 만한 계획이 필요하다.
noteKo.usage: a credible offer/threat 형태로 자주 쓴다.

current.ex: The current rules are too strict.

deal.ex: The two sides reached a deal.

delegation.en: a group sent to represent others
delegation.ex: A delegation from Japan visited the school.

deliberations.ex: The jury began its deliberations on Monday.

example.en: After two days of deliberations, the panel reached a decision.
example.zh: 經過兩天審議，小組作出了決定。

note.usage: 多用複數；jury/committee deliberations；after much deliberation。

noteEs.exampleTr: Tras dos días de deliberaciones, el comité decidió.

noteHi.exampleTr: दो दिन के विचार-विमर्श के बाद पैनल ने फ़ैसला किया।

noteJa.exampleTr: 2日間の審議の末、委員会は結論を出した。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이틀간의 심의 끝에 위원회가 결정을 내렸다.

department.ex: The Department of Education sets the rules.

described.ex: He described the hotel as quiet and clean.

determined.ex: The fine will be determined later.

differences.en: ways things are not the same
differences.ex: There are big price differences between shops.

discussion.ex: The plan is still under discussion.

discussions.ex: Discussions about the new park continue.

disparity.ex: The disparity between their salaries is huge.

example.en: There is a wide disparity in income between the two regions.
example.zh: 兩個地區之間的收入差距很大。

note.meaning: 差距；不均等。文中指男女在意外傷害上損失壽命的差距。
note.usage: 可數名詞；a disparity between A and B、disparity in + 名詞（income/health）；常帶「不公平」意味。

noteEn.meaning: a large difference between two groups, often seen as unfair.
noteEn.usage: 'a disparity between A and B', 'disparity in income/health'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Hay una gran disparidad de ingresos entre las dos regiones.
noteEs.meaning: gran diferencia entre grupos, a menudo injusta.
noteEs.usage: a disparity between A and B; disparity in income.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों क्षेत्रों की आय में बड़ा अंतर है।
noteHi.meaning: दो समूहों के बीच बड़ा, अक्सर अनुचित अंतर।
noteHi.usage: a disparity between A and B; disparity in income।

noteJa.exampleTr: 2つの地域の間には大きな所得格差がある。
noteJa.meaning: 2つの集団の大きな差、しばしば不公平な差。
noteJa.usage: a disparity between A and B、disparity in income。

noteKo.exampleTr: 두 지역 간 소득 격차가 크다.
noteKo.meaning: 두 집단 간의 큰, 종종 불공평한 차이; 격차.
noteKo.usage: a disparity between A and B, disparity in income.

dispute.ex: The pay dispute lasted three months.

disrupt.ja: 混乱させる；支障をきたす

distant.ex: A deal is a distant hope.

draft.en: an early version of a plan
draft.ex: The draft will be discussed next week.

due.en: expected to happen at a set time
due.ex: The report is due to come out on Friday.

duration.ex: You must stay in your seat for the duration of the flight.

during.en: throughout or at a point in a time

earlier.en: before the usual or expected time

effect.ex: The new rule had a big effect on prices.

employees.en: people who work for a company

ended.ex: The club ended its deal with the sponsor.

endorsement.ex: The plan won the endorsement of the board.

engagement.ex: Close engagement with parents helps schools.

enough.ex: He didn't run fast enough to catch the bus.

erosion.en: slow loss or weakening over time
erosion.ex: The erosion of trust is hard to fix.

example.en: Rising prices caused an erosion of savings.
example.zh: 物價上漲使儲蓄逐漸縮水。

note.usage: 原指土壤被侵蝕，引申為價值、權利逐漸減少；常見 erosion of pay/trust。

noteEn.meaning: a slow loss or weakening of something.
noteEn.usage: Used for value or rights: 'erosion of pay'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La subida de precios causó una erosión de los ahorros.
noteEs.usage: Pérdida lenta de valor o derechos: erosion of pay/trust.

noteHi.exampleTr: बढ़ती कीमतों से बचत का क्षरण हुआ।
noteHi.meaning: धीरे-धीरे घटना या कमज़ोर होना; क्षरण।
noteHi.usage: मूल्य या अधिकारों की धीमी कमी के लिए: erosion of pay/trust।

noteJa.exampleTr: 物価上昇で貯金が目減りした。
noteJa.usage: 価値や権利が少しずつ失われること。erosion of pay/trust。

noteKo.usage: 가치나 권리가 서서히 줄어드는 것: erosion of pay/trust.

evening.en: the end of the day before night

excess.ex: Bags in excess of 20kg cost extra.

expected.ex: The new park is expected to open in May.
expected.ja: 予想された；見込まれる

expressed.ex: Many people expressed concern about the plan.

facilitate.en: to make something easier to happen
facilitate.ex: The new app will facilitate online bookings.

example.en: The new rules will facilitate the transfer of technology.
example.zh: 新規定將有助於技術移轉。

note.meaning: 促進；使…更容易進行。文中指設在工業區讓日後移轉民間更方便。
note.usage: facilitate + 名詞（facilitate a transfer）；不說 facilitate sb to do。

noteEn.meaning: to make something easier to happen.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las nuevas normas facilitarán la transferencia de tecnología.
noteEs.meaning: hacer que algo sea más fácil.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए नियम तकनीक के हस्तांतरण को आसान बनाएँगे।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい規則は技術移転を容易にする。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 규정은 기술 이전을 쉽게 할 것이다.

failed.en: did not do what was expected
failed.ex: He failed to call his mother.

far.en: a long distance; far from: not at all
far.ex: They live far from the city.

faster.ex: Prices are rising faster than wages.

feasible.ex: The plan is not financially feasible.

figures.ex: The latest figures show a rise.

final.ex: The final decision is next week.

finance.ex: She works in finance at a big bank.

follow-up.en: done later to check or continue something
follow-up.ex: The doctor booked a follow-up visit.
follow-up.ja: 追跡の；フォローアップの

for.en: used to show purpose or who/what receives something

fortnight.ex: We are going on holiday for a fortnight.

forward.ex: He put forward a new idea.

fraught.ex: The plan is fraught with risk.

fresh.ex: The team needs a fresh approach.

from.en: used to show where something starts; stop from = prevent

further.en: at or to a greater distance
further.ex: The new market is further east than the old one.

gap.ex: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

general.en: general secretary: leader of a union
general.ex: The general secretary spoke to reporters.

get.ex: You can get a free shot at the clinic.

give.ex: Good taxes give the State more choice.

go.en: to move or be sent to a place
go.ex: The paintings will go to a gallery.

good.ex: There is some good news today.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: This group of patients needs special care.

had.en: past of have; (had to) were required to
had.ex: We had to wait an hour for the bus.
had.ja: 〜しなければならなかった；持っていた

half.ex: The trip took a year and a half.
half.ja: 半分；（a decade and a half）15年
half.zh: 一半；（a decade and a half）十五年

hamper.en: to make it harder for something to happen
hamper.ex: Bad weather may hamper the rescue work.

has.en: possesses; also used to form perfect tenses
has.ex: The town has two parks and a library.

have.en: to possess or suffer from; also used to form perfect tenses
have.ex: Many children have colds in winter.

having.en: used to form a perfect participle
having.ex: Having finished dinner, we went for a walk.

head.en: leader; (in place names) a point of land
head.ex: She is head of the sales team.

heads.en: leads or is in charge of

health.en: the state of being well; the health system
health.ex: Exercise is good for your health.
health.zh: 衛生；健康（Department of Health：衛生部）

heart.en: the central and most important part
heart.ex: The market is in the heart of the city.

heated.en: full of strong feelings and anger

hit.ex: Prices hit a new high last month.

hold.en: to organise and have an event
hold.ex: They will hold a meeting tomorrow.

hope.ex: We hope to finish the work today.

hoped.ex: She hoped to win the race.

hopeful.en: feeling that good things may happen
hopeful.ex: Doctors are hopeful she will recover.

hospitals.en: places where sick people are treated

hour.ex: The train leaves in an hour.

however.ex: It was cold; however, we still went swimming.

imminently.ex: The new law will take effect imminently.

impasse.en: a situation where no progress is possible
impasse.ex: The talks have reached an impasse.

example.en: The two sides finally broke the impasse after midnight.
example.zh: 雙方終於在午夜後打破了僵局。

note.meaning: 雙方無法達成共識、事情無法推進的僵局。
note.usage: 常用 reach an impasse（陷入僵局）、break the impasse（打破僵局）；正式用語。

noteEn.meaning: a situation where people cannot agree and nothing can move forward.
noteEn.usage: Common phrases: "reach an impasse" and "break the impasse".

noteEs.exampleTr: Las dos partes por fin rompieron el punto muerto pasada la medianoche.
noteEs.meaning: situación en la que no hay acuerdo y no se puede avanzar.
noteEs.usage: Se dice reach an impasse (llegar a un punto muerto) y break the impasse (desbloquearlo); es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों पक्षों ने आख़िरकार आधी रात के बाद गतिरोध तोड़ा।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी स्थिति जहाँ दोनों पक्ष सहमत नहीं होते और प्रगति रुक जाती है; गतिरोध।
noteHi.usage: reach an impasse (गतिरोध में फँसना), break the impasse (गतिरोध तोड़ना); औपचारिक शब्द।

noteJa.exampleTr: 両者は真夜中過ぎにようやく行き詰まりを打開した。
noteJa.meaning: 合意できず、物事が先に進まない行き詰まりの状態。
noteJa.usage: reach an impasse（行き詰まる）、break the impasse（打開する）の形で使う。硬い語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 양측은 자정이 넘어서야 마침내 교착 상태를 깼다.
noteKo.meaning: 합의가 되지 않아 일이 진척되지 않는 교착 상태.
noteKo.usage: reach an impasse(교착 상태에 빠지다), break the impasse(교착 상태를 깨다)로 쓰는 격식어.

in.en: inside; during; within a place, time or group

increase.ex: There was a sharp increase in prices.

inflation.ex: High inflation makes food more expensive.

inflationary.en: causing or linked to a general rise in prices
inflationary.ex: Higher wages can have an inflationary effect.
inflationary.zh: 通膨的；造成物價上漲的

insiders.en: people who know a business from inside
insiders.ex: Insiders say the bank will close two branches.

intensive.en: involving a lot of effort in a short time
intensive.ex: She took an intensive English course.

into.en: to the inside of; changing to become something

irish.zh: 愛爾蘭的；The Irish Times：《愛爾蘭時報》

jump.en: to rise suddenly by a large amount

justify.en: to give a good reason for something
justify.ex: Can you justify the high cost?

key.ex: Trust is a key part of any friendship.

last.ex: The meeting could last two hours.

lasted.en: continued for a period of time

late.en: near the end of the day

latest.ex: Have you read her latest book?

latter.ex: The latter half of the film was better.

lead.ex: She is the research lead on the project.

leaders.ex: World leaders met to discuss climate change.

leading.ex: Smoking is a leading cause of lung disease.

leads.en: is in charge of a group
leads.ex: She leads a team of ten.

lengthy.ex: After a lengthy delay, the train finally left.

lie.en: to be found in a place
lie.ex: Many dangers lie beneath the surface.

lifetime.ex: The plan has a lifetime of three years.

local.en: in or affecting a nearby small area

long.en: measuring a great length; (adv.) for a long time
long.ex: The bridge is two kilometres long.

lost.ex: The firm lost €2 million last year.

lot.ex: She drinks a lot of water every day.

made.en: achieved or produced (past participle of make)
made.ex: We have made good progress on the report this week.
made.zh: 取得；做出（make 的過去分詞）

maintain.en: to keep something at the same level
maintain.ex: We want to maintain good quality.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

means.ex: Staff means everyone who works here.

members.en: people who belong to a group

minimum.ex: There is a minimum age of 18.

minister.en: a leader of a government department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new school.

money.en: coins and notes used to buy things
money.ex: She saved money for a new bike.

month.en: one of the 12 parts of a year
month.ex: I visit my parents once a month.

more.en: a larger amount or number (more than)

morning.en: the early part of the day

move.en: an action taken to achieve something (n.); to go from place to place (v.)
move.ex: Cutting bus fares was a popular move.

must.ex: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.

national.ex: The team won the national championship last year.

necessitate.ex: The new rules will necessitate extra staff.

negotiations.en: formal talks to reach an agreement

negotiator.en: a person who discusses to reach an agreement
negotiator.ex: She is the union's chief negotiator.

negotiators.en: people who discuss to reach an agreement

neither.en: not one and not the other of two

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: She bought a new coat for winter.

night.en: the time when it is dark
night.ex: We saw the stars at night.

not.ex: I am not ready to leave yet.

notably.en: clearly; in a way people notice
notably.ex: The weather was notably warmer this week.

notice.en: a warning or information that something will happen
notice.ex: We got a notice about the change.

november.en: the eleventh month of the year

of.en: belonging to; showing a part or amount

off.en: away in time; (set off) to cause to start
off.ex: The holidays are still a long way off.

offer.ex: Many families offer rooms to students.

officials.en: people with positions of authority in government
officials.ex: City officials will announce the results tomorrow.

on.en: used for days, dates and topics

one-day.ex: We went on a one-day trip to the coast.

optimism.en: a feeling that good things will happen
optimism.ex: There is new optimism about the economy.

order.en: in order to: so that you can
order.ex: She studied hard in order to pass.

out.en: used in phrases like carried out, wipe out
out.ex: The work was carried out last year.
out.zh: 出（carried out：進行；wipe out：清除；locked out：拒於門外）

overnight.ex: A warning may be issued overnight.

part.ex: Teachers will take part in the strike.

participants.en: people who take part in something

participated.ex: Over 200 runners participated in the event.

parties.en: the groups taking part in talks

past.ex: Life was harder in the past.

pay.ex: The government will pay for the new hospital.

people.ex: Many people live in the city.

place.ex: This is a quiet place to read.

plan.en: to decide what to do in the future
plan.ex: We plan to visit Cork next summer.

pm.en: after midday; in the afternoon or evening

poised.en: ready and about to do something
poised.ex: The team is poised to win its first title.

position.ex: The union's position has not changed.

positions.en: views or opinions on an issue

postponed.ex: The match was postponed because of snow.

preceding.ex: Sales rose compared with the preceding month.

predicated.ex: The plan is predicated on good weather.

example.en: The plan is predicated on steady economic growth.
example.zh: 這項計畫是以經濟穩定成長為前提的。

paragraphs: Talks about pay for public workers ended on Friday night. There was no deal.
Union leaders and Government officials talked for about two weeks. They met at the Workplace Relations Commission.
Kevin Callinan leads the unions in the talks. He said the two sides are stuck. He said the Government has not made a good offer.
The unions want pay to go up with prices. Prices have gone up a lot in the last five years.
Workers had a one-day strike earlier this month. Now the unions may plan a second strike on 11 November. More than 300,000 workers could stop work. Schools would close.
The unions will meet on Monday. Some people still hope for a deal soon.

paragraphs: Talks on a new pay deal for public sector workers ended late on Friday night without an agreement. The talks had gone on for about two weeks.
Senior officials from the Department of Public Expenditure and union leaders met at the Workplace Relations Commission. They started at 10am on Friday and left at about 11pm.

Kevin Callinan, the head of the union Fórsa, leads the union side. He said the talks had reached an impasse, which means neither side can move forward. He said the talks were long and sometimes angry. He also said the Government had not yet made a believable offer.

The unions want three main things. First, they want workers to get back the money they lost because prices rose faster than pay over the past five years. Second, they want a pay rise for the second half of this year. Third, they want protection if prices jump again during a new deal.

More than 300,000 public sector workers went on strike for 24 hours earlier in October. A second strike was put on hold so that talks could continue. However, many workers are still following a work-to-rule, which means they do only the tasks in their contracts.

The 19 unions in the public services group will meet on Monday morning. If there is still no deal, they may hold a second national strike on Wednesday, 11 November. Schools would close, and hospitals and local councils would be affected. The unions must give seven days' notice.
On Thursday, Tánaiste Simon Harris said he hoped for a deal in the coming days. Some people close to the talks still believe an agreement is possible.

工會主要有三項訴求。
第一，他們希望員工能拿回過去五年因物價漲得比薪水快而損失的錢。

如果仍然沒有協議，他們可能會在11月11日週三舉行第二次全國罷工。

paragraphs: Negotiations between the Government and public sector unions on a new pay agreement broke up late on Friday night without a deal, after roughly two weeks of talks.

Senior officials from the Department of Public Expenditure and four leading union figures spent around 13 hours at the Workplace Relations Commission on Friday. However, sources said the two sides were not close enough to continue into the night.

Kevin Callinan, general secretary of Fórsa and the lead negotiator for the unions, said the process had reached an impasse. He described the talks as lengthy and at times heated, and said the Government had yet to put forward a credible offer. In his view, a deal that could be confidently recommended to members in a ballot was still a long way off.

The unions have set out three key demands. They want compensation for the gap between pay increases and inflation over the past five years, an increase covering the second half of this year, and protection against sudden rises in inflation during any new agreement.
More than 300,000 workers took part in a 24-hour strike earlier this month. A second stoppage was suspended to allow talks to proceed, but a work-to-rule remains in place across the public sector.

The 19 unions on the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions will meet on Monday. If no agreement is in sight, they are expected to schedule a second national strike for Wednesday, 11 November, which would close schools and disrupt health and council services. Seven days' notice is required.
Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris had said on Thursday that he was hopeful of a breakthrough within days, and some sources still believe a deal is within reach.

公共支出部的高級官員與四位主要工會人物週五在勞資關係委員會待了約13個小時。
然而，消息人士說雙方立場差距仍大，不值得談到深夜。
Fórsa秘書長、也是工會首席談判代表的凱文．卡利南表示，協商已陷入僵局。
他形容談判冗長且有時氣氛火爆，並說政府至今尚未提出可信的方案。
在他看來，一份能有信心推薦給會員投票表決的協議仍遙遙無期。
工會提出了三項主要訴求。
他們要求補償過去五年加薪幅度與通膨之間的差距、涵蓋今年下半年的加薪，以及在任何新協議期間對通膨突然上升的保障。
本月稍早，超過30萬名員工參與了24小時罷工。
第二次停工已暫停以便談判進行，但整個公部門仍持續「依法工作」。
愛爾蘭工會大會公共服務委員會的19個工會將於週一開會。
若協議仍無望，預料他們將把第二次全國罷工定在11月11日週三，屆時學校將停課，醫療與地方議會服務也會受到干擾。
依規定須提前七天通知。
副總理兼財政部長西蒙．哈里斯週四曾表示，他對數日內取得突破抱持希望，一些消息人士也仍認為協議近在咫尺。

paragraphs: Negotiations on a new public sector pay accord collapsed late on Friday night, as union leaders and Government officials failed to bridge their differences after a fortnight of intensive talks.

The latest session at the Workplace Relations Commission stretched for roughly 13 hours, but those present concluded that the parties' positions were too far apart to justify negotiating through the night.

Fórsa's general secretary, Kevin Callinan, who heads the union delegation, conceded that the talks had hit an impasse. He characterised the discussions as protracted and occasionally fraught, and accused the Government of having yet to table a credible offer. A settlement that could be put to members with any confidence, he warned, remained a distant prospect.

At the heart of the dispute lie three demands: redress for the erosion of pay by inflation over the past five years, an increase for the latter half of this year, and safeguards against fresh inflationary spikes over the lifetime of any deal.

Earlier this month, upwards of 300,000 workers staged a 24-hour walkout. A follow-up strike was shelved to give negotiators breathing space, yet a work-to-rule continues to bite across the public service.

The 19 unions represented on the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions are due to convene on Monday. Should no draft agreement materialise, they are poised to set a second national stoppage for Wednesday, 11 November, which would shut schools and hamper health and local authority services. Notice must be served seven days in advance.
Only on Thursday, Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris voiced optimism that an accord could be clinched within days, and some insiders maintain that a deal is still attainable.

勞資關係委員會最新一輪會談拉長到約13小時，但在場者認為雙方立場相距太遠，不值得通宵談判。
率領工會代表團的Fórsa秘書長凱文．卡利南承認，談判已陷入僵局。
他形容這些討論曠日持久、偶爾劍拔弩張，並指責政府至今仍未端出可信的方案。
他警告，一份能有把握交付會員表決的和解方案仍遙不可及。
爭議的核心在於三項訴求：補償過去五年通膨對薪資的侵蝕、今年下半年的加薪，以及在任何協議有效期間防範通膨再度飆升的保障措施。
本月稍早，逾30萬名員工發動了24小時罷工。
後續罷工被擱置，好給談判人員喘息空間，但「依法工作」行動仍持續在整個公共服務體系產生影響。
在愛爾蘭工會大會公共服務委員會中有代表的19個工會預定週一召開會議。
若協議草案仍未出現，他們準備把第二次全國停工定在11月11日週三，屆時學校將關閉，醫療與地方政府服務也將受阻。
必須提前七天發出通知。

paragraphs: Negotiations concerning a new public sector pay agreement concluded late on Friday evening without a resolution, following approximately two weeks of sustained engagement between trade union representatives and Government officials.

Although the final session at the Workplace Relations Commission lasted some 13 hours, participants ultimately determined that the respective positions were insufficiently aligned to warrant further overnight discussion.

Kevin Callinan, general secretary of Fórsa and principal negotiator for the unions, acknowledged that the process had reached an impasse. He described the deliberations as prolonged and at times contentious, and asserted that the Government had not yet presented a credible proposal. Consequently, in his assessment, an agreement capable of securing members' endorsement in a ballot remained considerably distant.

The unions' position is predicated upon three principal demands: compensation for the disparity between wage growth and inflation over the preceding five years, an increase applicable to the second half of the current year, and substantial protection against inflationary surges throughout the duration of any new arrangement.

Earlier in October, in excess of 300,000 employees participated in a 24-hour strike. A subsequent stoppage was postponed in order to facilitate negotiations; nevertheless, a work-to-rule remains in effect throughout the public sector.

The 19 unions constituting the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions are scheduled to meet on Monday. In the absence of a draft agreement, a second national strike is anticipated on Wednesday, 11 November, which would necessitate school closures and significantly disrupt health and local authority services. A minimum of seven days' notice is required.

Notably, Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris had expressed optimism on Thursday that an agreement could be reached imminently, and certain sources maintain that a settlement remains feasible.
sentZh: 經過工會代表與政府官員約兩週的持續協商，有關公部門新薪資協議的談判於週五深夜結束，未能達成解決方案。
雖然勞資關係委員會的最後一輪會談持續約13小時，與會者最終判定雙方立場不夠一致，不足以支持再通宵討論。
Fórsa秘書長、工會首席談判代表凱文．卡利南承認，協商已陷入僵局。
他形容商議過程冗長且有時充滿爭議，並斷言政府尚未提出可信的提案。
因此，依他的評估，一份能在投票中獲得會員支持的協議仍相當遙遠。
工會的立場建立在三項主要訴求上：補償過去五年工資成長與通膨之間的落差、適用於今年下半年的加薪，以及在任何新安排的整個期間內對通膨激增提供充分保障。
十月稍早，超過30萬名員工參與了24小時罷工。
隨後的停工已延後以利談判進行；然而，整個公部門仍持續實施「依法工作」。
組成愛爾蘭工會大會公共服務委員會的19個工會預定於週一開會。
若沒有協議草案，預計將於11月11日週三舉行第二次全國罷工，屆時學校必須停課，醫療與地方政府服務也將嚴重受擾。
至少須提前七天通知。
